nodes.name: Peer layer
nodes.summary: Typed request methods over a raw Outbound channel, plus the DispatchContext back-channel protocols.
nodes.detail: Contains ClientPeer (typed sampling/elicitation/roots/ping methods), BaseContext (per-request context forwarded to handlers), and the Outbound/DispatchContext Protocol definitions used throughout the dispatcher layer.

nodes.name: JSON-RPC dispatch
nodes.summary: JSON-RPC message routing: correlation, request fanout, cancellation, progress, and the in-memory direct path.
nodes.detail: Three layers: dispatcher.py defines the Outbound/DispatchContext/Dispatcher Protocols and CallOptions TypedDict. jsonrpc_dispatcher.py is the production implementation over SessionMessage streams, owning request-id minting, in-flight tracking, peer cancel, and progress. direct_dispatcher.py is an in-process implementation for testing that calls handlers synchronously without serialization.

nodes.name: In-memory transport
nodes.summary: In-process client/server stream pairs and context-propagating stream wrappers.
nodes.detail: memory.py creates two bidirectional anyio memory stream pairs (one per direction) and yields them as (client_streams, server_streams) for use in tests and in-process embedding. _context_streams.py wraps the raw streams to snapshot and restore contextvars across task boundaries. _stream_protocols.py defines ReadStream and WriteStream Protocols that are satisfied by both raw memory streams and the wrappers.

nodes.name: Cross-cutting utilities
nodes.summary: Standalone helpers used across the client and server: errors, URI templates, path security, tool names, subscriptions, skills, and HTTP utilities.
nodes.detail: exceptions.py defines MCPError and subclasses. uri_template.py implements RFC 6570 URI Template (Levels 1-3, Level 4 explode for path operators) with both expansion and matching. path_security.py provides safe_join and traversal checks for resource handlers. tool_name_validation.py enforces SEP-986. subscriptions.py models the 2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen event vocabulary. skills.py models the SEP-2640 Skills extension wire types. _httpx_utils.py creates httpx2 clients with MCP defaults and handles origin-bound redirects.

nodes.name: Wire framing
nodes.summary: SessionMessage envelope and TransportContext metadata shared by all transports.
nodes.detail: message.py defines SessionMessage (JSONRPCMessage + MessageMetadata), ClientMessageMetadata (resumption token, per-request headers), and ServerMessageMetadata (related request id, SSE close callbacks, can_send_request verdict). transport_context.py defines the immutable TransportContext base dataclass that all transports subclass, carrying kind, can_send_request, and optional headers.

nodes.name: Outbound
nodes.summary: Protocol for anything that can send requests and notifications to the peer.
nodes.detail: Runtime-checkable Protocol with two methods: send_raw_request(method, params, opts) -> dict and notify(method, params, opts) -> None. Satisfied by Dispatcher (top-level), DispatchContext (back-channel), and BaseContext (request context). The MCP typed layer builds on top of this raw channel.

nodes.name: DispatchContext
nodes.summary: Per-request context handed to on_request / on_notify with transport metadata and back-channel.
nodes.detail: Protocol extending Outbound. Carries transport (TransportContext), can_send_request, request_id, message_metadata, cancel_requested (anyio.Event), and progress(). send_raw_request raises NoBackChannelError when can_send_request is False. Concrete implementation is _JSONRPCDispatchContext inside jsonrpc_dispatcher.py.

nodes.name: CallOptions
nodes.summary: Per-call options TypedDict for send_raw_request: request_id, timeout, cancel_on_abandon, on_progress, resumption_token, headers.
nodes.detail: Total=False TypedDict. Key fields: request_id (caller-supplied id; collisions raise ValueError), timeout (seconds before REQUEST_TIMEOUT), cancel_on_abandon (whether to send notifications/cancelled on timeout/caller-cancel; default True), on_progress (ProgressFnT callback), resumption_token and on_resumption_token (streamable-HTTP only, 2025-11-25 and earlier), headers (merged by HTTP transports).

nodes.name: Dispatcher
nodes.summary: Protocol for a full duplex request/notification channel with call-return semantics.
nodes.detail: Extends Outbound. Adds run(on_request, on_notify, on_notify_intercept, task_status). Implementations own request-id correlation, the receive loop, per-request concurrency, and cancellation/progress wiring. JSONRPCDispatcher is the production implementation; DirectDispatcher is the in-memory alternative.

nodes.name: JSONRPCDispatcher
nodes.summary: Production JSON-RPC dispatcher over the SessionMessage stream pair, owning all correlation and cancel logic.
nodes.detail: Wraps read_stream/write_stream of SessionMessage. Maintains _pending dict (request_id -> _Pending with response channel) and _in_flight dict (request_id -> _InFlight with cancel scope). run() starts the receive loop in a task group and calls task_status.started(). _dispatch() routes each message: responses resolve _pending waiters; requests spawn _handle_request; notifications intercept progress/cancel then spawn on_notify. send_raw_request mints ids, creates per-request memory streams (buffer=1), injects OTel trace context, writes the request, then awaits the response. Handler exceptions are normalized to MCPError.
nodes.code:
async def _dispatch_request(self, req, metadata, on_request, sender_ctx):
    progress_token = progress_token_from_params(req.params)
    dctx = _JSONRPCDispatchContext(
        transport=transport_ctx,
        _dispatcher=self,
        _request_id=req.id,
        message_metadata=metadata,
        _progress_token=progress_token,
    )
    scope = anyio.CancelScope()
    self._in_flight[coerce_request_id(req.id)] = _InFlight(scope=scope, dctx=dctx)
    self._spawn(self._handle_request, req, dctx, scope, on_request, sender_ctx=sender_ctx)

nodes.name: JSONRPCDispatcher.run()
nodes.summary: Drive the receive loop until the read stream closes, then wake all pending waiters with CONNECTION_CLOSED.
nodes.detail: Opens a task group; sets _running=True and calls task_status.started(). Iterates the read stream, calling _dispatch() for each item. On EOF or ClosedResourceError, calls _fan_out_closed() to wake _pending waiters. Cancels the task group on exit so in-flight handlers are stopped. Single-shot: cannot be restarted.
nodes.signature: async def run(self, on_request, on_notify, on_notify_intercept=None, *, task_status=TASK_STATUS_IGNORED) -> None

nodes.name: JSONRPCDispatcher.send_raw_request()
nodes.summary: Send a JSON-RPC request, await its response or timeout, and send a courtesy cancel on abandon.
nodes.detail: Mints or validates request_id (with coerce_request_id), creates a _Pending with buffer-1 memory stream, writes JSONRPCRequest, starts the request_clock, awaits receive(). On timeout or caller-cancel, sends notifications/cancelled via _final_write (shielded on cancel). Raises MCPError(REQUEST_TIMEOUT) on timeout, MCPError(CONNECTION_CLOSED) on EOF.
nodes.signature: async def send_raw_request(self, method, params, opts=None, *, _related_request_id=None) -> dict[str, Any]
nodes.code:
send, receive = anyio.create_memory_object_stream[dict[str, Any] | ErrorData](1)
pending = _Pending(send=send, receive=receive, on_progress=on_progress)
self._pending[pending_key] = pending
plan = _plan_outbound(_related_request_id, opts)
request_write_started = False
timeout_armed = False
with otel_span(span_name, kind=SpanKind.CLIENT, ...) as span:
    inject_trace_context(out_meta)
    await self._write(msg, plan.metadata)
    clock.start()
    timeout_armed = True
    outcome = await receive.receive()

nodes.name: handler_exception_to_error_data()
nodes.summary: Map MCPError to its ErrorData and ValidationError to INVALID_PARAMS; return None for anything else.
nodes.detail: Shared by JSONRPCDispatcher and the modern HTTP entry point. MCPError carries its own ErrorData directly. pydantic ValidationError maps to INVALID_PARAMS with empty data (no pydantic text on the wire). Any other exception returns None so each caller applies its own catch-all; JSONRPCDispatcher currently pins code=0 for v1 compat.

nodes.name: coerce_request_id()
nodes.summary: Coerce a stringified integer request id to int so peer-echoed ids still correlate.
nodes.detail: Shared by JSONRPCDispatcher and DirectDispatcher. The TypeScript SDK may stringify numeric ids; this ensures '7' and 7 hit the same _pending bucket. Applied to both inbound response ids (in _resolve_pending) and to the pending-key for caller-supplied ids.

nodes.name: DirectDispatcher
nodes.summary: In-process Dispatcher that calls a peer's on_request directly, with no serialization.
nodes.detail: Two DirectDispatchers are wired together by create_direct_dispatcher_pair. send_raw_request calls peer._dispatch_request, which invokes the peer's on_request synchronously in-process. run() parks until close() is called. Exception mapping mirrors JSONRPCDispatcher: MCPError passes through, ValidationError -> INVALID_PARAMS, others -> INTERNAL_ERROR (chained when raise_handler_exceptions=True). Used in tests and for in-process server embedding.

nodes.name: create_direct_dispatcher_pair()
nodes.summary: Create a (client, server) pair of DirectDispatchers wired to each other.
nodes.detail: Creates one shared TransportContext (kind='direct', can_send_request=can_send_request), two DirectDispatchers sharing it, and cross-wires them with connect_to. The pairing is symmetric: either side can initiate requests. Used by tests that want the dispatcher layer without JSON-RPC overhead.
nodes.signature: def create_direct_dispatcher_pair(*, can_send_request=True, headers=None, raise_handler_exceptions=True) -> tuple[DirectDispatcher, DirectDispatcher]
nodes.code:
ctx = TransportContext(kind=DIRECT_TRANSPORT_KIND, can_send_request=can_send_request, headers=headers)
client = DirectDispatcher(ctx, raise_handler_exceptions=raise_handler_exceptions)
server = DirectDispatcher(ctx, raise_handler_exceptions=raise_handler_exceptions)
client.connect_to(server)
server.connect_to(client)
return client, server

nodes.name: create_client_server_memory_streams()
nodes.summary: Async context manager that yields paired bidirectional memory streams for in-process client/server testing.
nodes.detail: Creates two pairs of anyio ContextSendStream/ContextReceiveStream (server-to-client and client-to-server). Yields ((client_read, client_write), (server_read, server_write)). All four streams are opened as context managers so they close atomically on exit. Calls resync_tracer() after close to work around the CPython 3.11 tracing bug.
nodes.signature: @asynccontextmanager async def create_client_server_memory_streams() -> AsyncGenerator[tuple[MessageStream, MessageStream], None]
nodes.code:
server_to_client_send, server_to_client_receive = create_context_streams[SessionMessage | Exception](1)
client_to_server_send, client_to_server_receive = create_context_streams[SessionMessage | Exception](1)
client_streams = (server_to_client_receive, client_to_server_send)
server_streams = (client_to_server_receive, server_to_client_send)
async with server_to_client_receive, client_to_server_send, client_to_server_receive, server_to_client_send:
    yield client_streams, server_streams

nodes.name: ContextSendStream
nodes.summary: Send-side wrapper that snapshots contextvars.copy_context() on every send().
nodes.detail: Wraps MemoryObjectSendStream[_Envelope[T]]. Each call to send(item) captures the current context via copy_context() and sends (context, item) as an envelope. The receive side extracts it via last_context. Needed so ASGI middleware contextvars (auth, OTel) set on the writer's task propagate to the spawned handler.

nodes.name: ContextReceiveStream
nodes.summary: Receive-side wrapper that unpacks the envelope and exposes the sender's context in last_context.
nodes.detail: Wraps MemoryObjectReceiveStream[_Envelope[T]]. receive() unpacks (ctx, item) and sets self.last_context = ctx, then returns item. Consumers call last_context via getattr to stay duck-type compatible with plain streams. __anext__ raises StopAsyncIteration on EndOfStream for async-for compatibility.

nodes.name: SessionMessage
nodes.summary: Transport envelope: a JSONRPCMessage paired with optional MessageMetadata.
nodes.detail: Dataclass with two fields: message (JSONRPCMessage from mcp_types) and metadata (MessageMetadata = ClientMessageMetadata | ServerMessageMetadata | None). All transports produce and consume this type. The metadata carries transport-specific routing: resumption tokens on the client side, related_request_id and SSE-stream callbacks on the server side.

nodes.name: TransportContext
nodes.summary: Immutable base dataclass for transport-specific metadata attached to each inbound message.
nodes.detail: Frozen kw_only dataclass. Fields: kind (str, e.g. 'stdio', 'streamable-http', 'direct'), can_send_request (bool - False for three reasons: no room in response, no session, or 2026-07-28 protocol forbids server-initiated requests), headers (Mapping[str, str] | None, populated by HTTP transports). Each transport subclasses this and adds its own fields; the dispatcher passes it opaquely.

nodes.name: MCPError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when an error arrives over an MCP connection; wraps ErrorData.
nodes.detail: Stores an ErrorData on self.error. Properties code, message, data delegate to it. Factory methods from_jsonrpc_error and from_error_data parse wire errors. __str__ returns message. Raised by dispatchers on peer error responses, timeouts (REQUEST_TIMEOUT), and connection close (CONNECTION_CLOSED).

nodes.name: NoBackChannelError
nodes.summary: MCPError subclass raised when a server-initiated request has no channel that can deliver it.
nodes.detail: Serializes to INVALID_REQUEST. Raised by DispatchContext.send_raw_request when TransportContext.can_send_request is False, and by a connection's standalone channel when it has none. The method name is embedded in the message for diagnostics.

nodes.name: UrlElicitationRequiredError
nodes.summary: MCPError for when a tool handler requires URL-mode elicitation(s) before proceeding.
nodes.detail: Code is URL_ELICITATION_REQUIRED. Carries a list of ElicitRequestURLParams in error.data['elicitations']. from_error() reconstructs from wire ErrorData. Servers raise this from tool handlers; clients detect it and present the URL flows before retrying.

nodes.name: ClientPeer
nodes.summary: Typed server-to-client request methods (sample, elicit_form, elicit_url, list_roots, ping) over a wrapped Outbound.
nodes.detail: Wraps any Outbound and exposes typed methods. sample is deprecated as of 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577). list_roots is deprecated similarly. elicit_form sends 'elicitation/create' with ElicitRequestFormParams; elicit_url sends URL-mode elicitation. ping sends a 'ping' request and ignores the result. All methods serialize params via dump_params (which handles _meta merging and alias translation).

nodes.name: dump_params()
nodes.summary: Serialize a params model to a wire dict, merging meta into _meta with alias translation.
nodes.detail: Shared by ClientPeer and Connection. model_dump(by_alias=True, mode='json', exclude_none=True) produces the wire dict. If meta is provided, it is serialized through RequestParams so Python field names (e.g. progress_token) emit their wire aliases (progressToken). Meta keys take precedence over any existing _meta on the model.
nodes.signature: def dump_params(model: BaseModel | None, meta: Meta | None = None) -> dict[str, Any] | None

nodes.name: BaseContext
nodes.summary: Per-request context wrapping a DispatchContext; exposes transport, cancel_requested, back-channel, and progress.
nodes.detail: Generic over TransportT (bound TransportContext). Constructed by ServerRunner per inbound request. Properties transport, cancel_requested, can_send_request, meta delegate to self._dctx. send_raw_request and notify proxy to _dctx. report_progress calls _dctx.progress(). Satisfies Outbound so ClientPeer can wrap it. Server's Context extends this with lifespan/connection; ClientContext is an alias.

nodes.name: classify_inbound_request()
nodes.summary: Run the three-rung modern-protocol validation ladder over a decoded JSON-RPC body.
nodes.detail: Rung 1: params._meta must carry protocol version and client capabilities. Rung 2 (HTTP only): MCP-Protocol-Version header matches body version, Mcp-Method matches method, Mcp-Name matches the name param for tools/call, prompts/get, resources/read. Rung 3: protocol version is a string in supported_modern_versions. Returns InboundModernRoute on success, InboundLadderRejection on the first failure. Method existence is not a rung.

nodes.name: encode_header_value()
nodes.summary: Wrap a value in =?base64?...?= sentinel when it would not survive an HTTP field round-trip.
nodes.detail: Plain printable ASCII that does not look like the sentinel passes verbatim. Control chars, non-ASCII, edge whitespace, or values that already look like the sentinel are base64-encoded. Inverse is decode_header_value which rejects non-canonical base64 and malformed UTF-8 by returning None.

nodes.name: UriTemplate
nodes.summary: RFC 6570 URI Template supporting Levels 1-3 and Level 4 explode for path operators, with bidirectional expand/match.
nodes.detail: expand(variables) substitutes variables and returns the URI string. match(uri) is the inverse: it recovers the variable bindings from a concrete URI. Matching uses a two-ended O(n*v) scan that never backtracks, with at most one multi-segment variable per template (more would be ambiguous). Templates with adjacent unanchored variables are rejected at parse time. Length limits: DEFAULT_MAX_TEMPLATE_LENGTH=8192, DEFAULT_MAX_VARIABLES=256, DEFAULT_MAX_URI_LENGTH=65536.

nodes.name: safe_join()
nodes.summary: Join path components onto a base, raising PathEscapeError on null bytes, absolute injection, or symlink escape.
nodes.detail: Resolves base and target via Path.resolve(), then checks target.is_relative_to(base_resolved). Catches null bytes (rejected before joining), absolute components (would silently discard base in Path's / operator), and post-resolve escapes including symlinks. The symlink check is point-in-time; callers in concurrent trees should use O_NOFOLLOW additionally.
nodes.signature: def safe_join(base: str | Path, *parts: str) -> Path

nodes.name: ServerEvent
nodes.summary: Union type for the four 2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen event kinds: tools, prompts, resources list changes, and resource updated.
nodes.detail: Four frozen dataclasses: ToolsListChanged, PromptsListChanged, ResourcesListChanged (no fields), ResourceUpdated (uri: str). event_to_notification converts to the wire notification format with _meta stamped. event_from_wire parses raw method+params pairs. event_matches applies a SubscriptionFilter to decide delivery. LISTEN_STREAM_METHODS is the frozenset of notification methods that ride listen streams.

nodes.name: Skill
nodes.summary: SEP-2640 Skills extension: one entry returned by skills/list or skills/get, with conformance checks at construction.
nodes.detail: Model with uri (SKILL.md resource URI), frontmatter (dict), resources (list[SkillResource] | 'dynamic'), _meta. _check_conformance validator ensures frontmatter name matches the URI's skill name, description is 1-1024 chars, all resource URIs are within the skill directory with no duplicates and SKILL.md present. MAX_RESOURCES_PER_SKILL=512 and MAX_TOTAL_SIZE=16MiB are SHOULD NOT limits, not hard caps.

nodes.name: create_mcp_http_client()
nodes.summary: Create an httpx2 AsyncClient with 30s connect/write/pool timeout and 300s read timeout for SSE streams.
nodes.detail: Default timeout is httpx2.Timeout(30.0, read=300.0). Redirect following is disabled; MCP transports follow redirects themselves via stream_within_origin. Returns an AsyncClient that must be used as a context manager.

nodes.name: stream_within_origin()
nodes.summary: Async context manager streaming a request and following redirects only within the same origin.
nodes.detail: Builds the request then loops: sends with follow_redirects=False, checks next_request_within_origin. Follows 307/308 and GET redirects within the same scheme+host+port (or http-to-https upgrade on default ports). Any cross-origin redirect, or one past client.max_redirects, yields the redirect response as-is. Used by all MCP HTTP transports.
nodes.signature: @asynccontextmanager async def stream_within_origin(client, method, url, **kwargs) -> AsyncGenerator[httpx2.Response]

nodes.name: request_clock()
nodes.summary: Context manager that installs a per-request timeout clock that only runs while waiting on the peer (not on a person).
nodes.detail: Creates a CancelScope and a RequestClock storing the remaining budget. The clock is placed in a ContextVar so transport code far below send_raw_request can find and pause it (waiting_on_a_person()). The clock starts only after the request write completes (clock.start()). After the scope exits, raises TimeoutError if cancelled_caught. Not public API; may change.

nodes.name: otel_span()
nodes.summary: Create an OpenTelemetry span around outbound MCP requests, injecting W3C trace context into _meta.
nodes.detail: otel_span creates a span via the shared _tracer ('mcp-python-sdk'). inject_trace_context injects traceparent/tracestate into the outbound _meta dict (SEP-414). extract_trace_context reads the same fields from an inbound _meta and returns a Context if valid. Used by JSONRPCDispatcher for outbound requests.
nodes.signature: @contextmanager def otel_span(name, *, kind, attributes=None, context=None, ...) -> Generator[Span]

nodes.name: get_display_name()
nodes.summary: Return the preferred display name for a Tool, Resource, Prompt, ResourceTemplate, or Implementation.
nodes.detail: For Tools: title > annotations.title > name. For all other types: title > name. Intended for client UIs; the title field is human-readable while name is the programmatic identifier.
nodes.signature: def get_display_name(obj: Tool | Resource | Prompt | ResourceTemplate | Implementation) -> str

nodes.name: validate_and_warn_tool_name()
nodes.summary: Validate a tool name against SEP-986 and log warnings for non-conforming names; return True if valid.
nodes.detail: Primary entry point. Calls validate_tool_name which checks: not empty, length <= 128, matches TOOL_NAME_REGEX (^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$). Warnings (not failures) for spaces, commas, leading/trailing dash or dot. Invalid characters produce a failure. Calls issue_tool_name_warning to log via the standard logger.

nodes.name: validate_extension_identifier()
nodes.summary: Raise TypeError unless identifier is a valid vendor-prefix/name string per SEP-2133.
nodes.detail: Pattern: dot-separated labels (each starting with a letter, ending with letter or digit, hyphens interior) + '/' + name (alphanumeric ends, dots/underscores/hyphens interior). Raises TypeError naming the owner for diagnostics.
nodes.signature: def validate_extension_identifier(identifier: Any, *, owner: str) -> None

nodes.name: is_async_callable()
nodes.summary: Return True if the callable is a coroutine function or has an async __call__ method.
nodes.detail: Strips functools.partial wrappers before checking. Checks inspect.iscoroutinefunction on obj and on obj.__call__. Adapted from Starlette's _utils. Used by the high-level server to decide whether to await a handler.

nodes.name: Package root (mcp)
nodes.summary: Public API surface: re-exports wire types from mcp_types, Client, ClientSession, ServerSession, MCPError, UriTemplate, and stdio helpers.
nodes.detail: __all__ lists 54 names. Wire types (CallToolRequest, ClientCapabilities, Tool, etc.) are re-exported directly from mcp_types. SDK types come from their home modules: Client from client.client, ClientSession from client.session, ServerSession from server.session, MCPError and UrlElicitationRequiredError from shared.exceptions, UriTemplate and InvalidUriTemplate from shared.uri_template, stdio_client and stdio_server from their respective transports. The mcp.types submodule is also bound for v1 backward compat.

nodes.name: CLI commands
nodes.summary: The mcp command: dev (Inspector), run (direct), and install (Claude Desktop registration) subcommands.
nodes.detail: Built on typer. dev launches npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector with a uv run command wrapping the server file. run imports and calls server.run(transport=...). install calls claude.update_claude_config to write the server entry into claude_desktop_config.json under mcpServers. All three parse file_spec as path[:object] and import the server via _import_server which looks for mcp/server/app module attributes. dotenv is an optional import for --env-file.

nodes.name: dev()
nodes.summary: Run an MCP server with the MCP Inspector via npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector.
nodes.detail: Builds a uv run command (_build_uv_command) that includes mcp[cli] pinned to the running SDK version via mcp_requirement(). Passes it to npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector. Uses shell=True on Windows. Exits with the subprocess returncode.

nodes.name: run()
nodes.summary: Import and run an MCP server directly in the current process.
nodes.detail: Calls _import_server then server.run(transport=transport). Note: only MCPServer is supported; low-level Server objects are rejected with a warning. No dependency management; callers should use 'mcp install' or 'mcp dev' for that.

nodes.name: install()
nodes.summary: Register an MCP server in Claude Desktop's config file.
nodes.detail: Resolves the server name, collects packages and env vars (from --env-var flags and optional --env-file via python-dotenv), then calls claude.update_claude_config. Existing env vars are preserved and merged; new values take precedence. Exits with error if Claude Desktop is not found.
nodes.signature: @app.command() def install(file_spec, server_name, with_editable, with_packages, env_vars, env_file) -> None

nodes.name: Claude Desktop integration
nodes.summary: Utilities to locate and write to Claude Desktop's configuration file (claude_desktop_config.json).
nodes.detail: get_claude_config_path() finds the config dir per platform: ~/AppData/Roaming/Claude on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Claude on macOS, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Claude on Linux. update_claude_config writes a mcpServers entry with uv run --frozen and the pinned mcp[cli] requirement. mcp_requirement() pins to the installed SDK version; dev/local versions fall back to unpinned.

nodes.name: update_claude_config()
nodes.summary: Add or update an MCP server entry in claude_desktop_config.json under mcpServers.
nodes.detail: Reads existing config JSON, preserves and merges env vars (existing vars kept, new ones take precedence), builds the uv run --frozen command with --with mcp[cli]==<version> and any additional packages (deduplicated), writes config back with json.dumps indent=2. Creates the file if absent. Returns bool success.
nodes.signature: def update_claude_config(file_spec, server_name, *, with_editable=None, with_packages=None, env_vars=None) -> bool

nodes.name: OS helpers
nodes.summary: Platform-specific process and file-handle utilities for the stdio transport.
nodes.detail: posix/utilities.py: terminate_posix_process_tree sends SIGTERM to the process group, polls for exit, then SIGKILLs survivors after a 2-second timeout. win32/utilities.py: create_windows_process spawns via anyio.open_process (with CREATE_NO_WINDOW) and assigns the process to a Windows Job Object so KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE reaps the entire tree. FallbackProcess wraps subprocess.Popen for SelectorEventLoop. rebind_std_handle_to_fd syncs the Win32 standard-handle slot after os.dup2 so subprocess handle inheritance sees the right file.

nodes.name: terminate_posix_process_tree()
nodes.summary: SIGTERM a process group, wait up to 2 seconds, then SIGKILL survivors.
nodes.detail: Uses os.killpg(pgid, SIGTERM) where pgid=process.pid (the leader; set via start_new_session). Polls _group_alive every 10ms within anyio.move_on_after(timeout_seconds). After the grace period, suppresses ESRCH/EPERM on SIGKILL since the group may have exited.
nodes.signature: async def terminate_posix_process_tree(process: Process, timeout_seconds: float = 2.0) -> None

nodes.name: create_windows_process()
nodes.summary: Spawn a Windows subprocess with CREATE_NO_WINDOW and assign it to a Job Object for tree termination.
nodes.detail: Tries anyio.open_process first; falls back to FallbackProcess (Popen-backed) on NotImplementedError (SelectorEventLoop). Creates a Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, then assigns the process via OpenProcess + AssignProcessToJobObject. Children spawned before assignment land outside the job; fix is CREATE_SUSPENDED spawn if needed.
nodes.signature: async def create_windows_process(command, args, env=None, errlog=sys.stderr, cwd=None) -> Process | FallbackProcess

nodes.name: FallbackProcess
nodes.summary: Async wrapper around subprocess.Popen for Windows event loops without async subprocess support.
nodes.detail: wait() polls Popen.poll() every 10ms instead of blocking (blocking defeats anyio cancellation). terminate() and kill() delegate to Popen. stdin and stdout are wrapped as anyio FileWriteStream / FileReadStream. Used when anyio.open_process raises NotImplementedError.

nodes.name: resync_tracer()
nodes.summary: Workaround for CPython 3.11 coverage tracing desync after a cancelled task-group join.
nodes.detail: Calls anyio.lowlevel.cancel_shielded_checkpoint() once to force a resume via .send() rather than .throw(), re-stamping the missing 'call' trace events. Needed in JSONRPCDispatcher.run, DirectDispatcher._dispatch_request, and create_client_server_memory_streams. Scheduled for removal when Python 3.11 support ends (EOL 2027-10).

nodes.name: validate_mcp_param_headers()
nodes.summary: Compare Mcp-Param-* headers against body arguments for a tools/call request.
nodes.detail: For each x-mcp-header annotated property in input_schema, checks that the header and argument agree: present together and equal after sentinel decoding, or absent together. Integer-typed with canonical decimal encoding compares numerically. A schema with an invalid x-mcp-header annotation validates nothing (conforming clients drop the tool). Returns InboundLadderRejection on the first mismatch, None on success.

nodes.name: ClientPeer.send_raw_request()
nodes.summary: Thin pass-through that delegates a raw JSON-RPC request to the wrapped Outbound.
nodes.detail: Delegates directly to self._outbound.send_raw_request(method, params, opts). Exists so callers can use a ClientPeer anywhere an Outbound is accepted without unpacking the wrapper.
nodes.signature: async def send_raw_request(self, method, params, opts=None) -> dict[str, Any]
nodes.code:
async def send_raw_request(
    self,
    method: str,
    params: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
    opts: CallOptions | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return await self._outbound.send_raw_request(method, params, opts)

nodes.name: ClientPeer.elicit_url()
nodes.summary: Send a URL-mode elicitation/create request carrying message, url, and elicitation_id.
nodes.detail: Builds ElicitRequestURLParams and calls send_raw_request('elicitation/create', ...). Returns ElicitResult validated from the peer's raw dict. Raises MCPError on peer error or NoBackChannelError when the transport has no back-channel.
nodes.signature: async def elicit_url(self, message, url, elicitation_id, *, meta=None, opts=None) -> ElicitResult
nodes.code:
async def elicit_url(
    self,
    message: str,
    url: str,
    elicitation_id: str,
    *,
    meta: Meta | None = None,
    opts: CallOptions | None = None,
) -> ElicitResult:
    params = ElicitRequestURLParams(message=message, url=url, elicitation_id=elicitation_id)
    result = await self.send_raw_request("elicitation/create", dump_params(params, meta), opts)
    return ElicitResult.model_validate(result, by_name=False)

nodes.name: skill_name_from_uri()
nodes.summary: Extract the skill name from a SKILL.md resource URI per SEP-2640.
nodes.detail: Splits the URI with urlsplit; validates it ends in /SKILL.md and has no query or fragment. For a URI with a path directory (organizational prefix), the name is the final path segment; for a bare skill://<name>/SKILL.md form it uses the hostname. Raises ValueError on malformed or nameless URIs.

nodes.name: parse_directory_uri()
nodes.summary: Split a directory resource URI into (scheme, netloc, path), rejecting trailing slashes.
nodes.detail: Validates no trailing slash and that the URI is absolute (has scheme, no query or fragment). Returns (scheme, netloc, path) for use in validate_directory_result. Raises ValueError on malformed URIs.
nodes.signature: def parse_directory_uri(uri: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]

nodes.name: UriTemplate.expand()
nodes.summary: Substitute variable values into the template and return the expanded URI string.
nodes.detail: Iterates the parsed _parts list; literal strings are appended verbatim, expression parts call _expand_expression which applies percent-encoding per operator (simple encodes reserved chars; + and # leave them intact). Absent variables are silently omitted per RFC 6570. Raises TypeError for non-string scalar values.
nodes.signature: def expand(self, variables: Mapping[str, str | Sequence[str]]) -> str

nodes.name: UriTemplate.match()
nodes.summary: Inverse of expand: match a concrete URI and return extracted variable bindings, or None.
nodes.detail: Uses a two-ended O(n*v) scan anchored on prefix literals and suffix literals, with at most one greedy multi-segment variable. Query variables at the end are matched leniently: order-agnostic, partial, unrecognized params ignored. Oversized inputs (> max_uri_length) return None immediately. Returns dict[str, str | list[str]]; explode variables yield list[str], others str.
nodes.signature: def match(self, uri: str, *, max_uri_length: int = DEFAULT_MAX_URI_LENGTH) -> dict[str, str | list[str]] | None

flows.name: Inbound JSON-RPC request routed to a handler
flows.summary: An inbound JSON-RPC message is parsed from the stream, matched to a pending response or dispatched to a handler, and the response is written back.

steps.text: The receive loop iterates the read stream. For each SessionMessage, _dispatch() is called in receive order.
Each item is a SessionMessage wrapping a JSONRPCMessage (request, response, notification, or error) and optional MessageMetadata (ServerMessageMetadata for HTTP, None for stdio/memory).
transport_builder is called on the metadata to produce a TransportContext. For ServerMessageMetadata, can_send_request is read from the metadata's own verdict; for other metadata it defaults to True.

For a JSONRPCRequest, _dispatch_request creates a _JSONRPCDispatchContext and an anyio.CancelScope, registers both in _in_flight under coerce_request_id(req.id), then spawns _handle_request in the task group (or awaits it inline for initialize). For notifications/cancelled and notifications/progress, the correlating entry in _in_flight or _pending is updated synchronously before on_notify is offered the message.
The server's runner wraps the DispatchContext in a BaseContext (or its server-side subclass Context) and passes it to the user's handler as the first argument.

If the handler raises MCPError, its ErrorData is written back as a JSONRPCError. A pydantic ValidationError maps to INVALID_PARAMS. Any other exception is mapped via handler_exception_to_error_data: currently code=0 for v1 compat. A peer-cancelled request is settled unanswered (no response written, transport notified via on_request_unanswered hook).

flows.name: In-memory client/server session for tests
flows.summary: create_client_server_memory_streams wires a server and client over in-memory streams, allowing in-process tests without serialization.

steps.text: create_client_server_memory_streams() creates two pairs of ContextSendStream / ContextReceiveStream (buffer size 1): one for each direction. It yields (client_streams, server_streams) where each is (read_stream, write_stream).

Every send() on a ContextSendStream snapshots the sender's contextvars via copy_context() and wraps the item in an envelope. This propagates ASGI middleware state (auth tokens, OTel spans) from the HTTP transport task to the handler task.

receive() on a ContextReceiveStream unwraps the envelope and stores the sender's context in last_context. JSONRPCDispatcher reads this attribute after each receive and passes the context to _spawn via Context.run, so the handler inherits the sender's contextvars.

Both client and server wrap their respective streams in a JSONRPCDispatcher. Each side calls run(on_request, on_notify) in a task group; task_status.started() signals readiness. send_raw_request on one side writes a JSONRPCRequest into the write stream; the other side's receive loop picks it up and dispatches it to the handler.

For tests that need even less overhead, create_direct_dispatcher_pair skips streams entirely: send_raw_request calls peer._dispatch_request directly in-process, sharing the same TransportContext. This eliminates serialization, context-snapshot overhead, and task-group scheduling, making tests faster and more deterministic.
